title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
authors: R. Schaeffer, B. Miranda, S. Koyejo
before: Sudden capability jumps with scale were widely accepted and used in safety arguments.
problem: The jumps were measured with all-or-nothing metrics like exact match.
breakthrough: Show that the same runs look smooth under continuous metrics, so the discontinuity may be in the ruler, not the model.
why: A rare, effective correction to a dominant narrative, and a caution about how capability claims are measured.
next: More careful evaluation methodology, and continuing disagreement about what emergence means.
inherits: Scepticism about benchmark discontinuities as evidence.
